Cool. I wonder why it looks like the waves in the high E string mostly go the opposite direction from the rest of the strings.

Probably something to do with the camera's frame-rate and the Hz that the string was vibrating at. Each frame catches the string moving a certain distance, that when pieced together gives the impression that it's going backwards, when it really isn't.

The strings don't move in uneven waves like that. They move in an almost perfect sine curve. The reason they appear that way in the video has to do with the camera's frame rate. The strings move so much in between the individual frames of the video, that the frames are unable to capture the entirety of their movement. Instead you get a strange "dancing in a strobe light" sense of their motion. This combined with the fact that the sensor in the camera records each frame rolling from left to right so that not all parts of a frame happened at exactly the same time (though it's within a very small fraction of a second, usually 1/24 to 1/60).
